core_obligations: Reduce to schemes (proof lines 626-638): since f is dominant the generic point of X maps to the generic point of Y; passing to the schematic loci of Y and of the preimage of Y' gives integral schemes containing those generic points, over which the morphism is locally of finite type, so the first three conditions are equivalent by the scheme case of the lemma.

Add quasi-finiteness (proof lines 640-648): condition (4) implies (1) by the comparison of transcendence degrees applied to the composite X -> Y -> Y, while (3) implies (4) because a finite morphism is quasi-finite and the generic point lies in U; hence (1)-(4) are equivalent.

The uniqueness condition (proof lines 650-658): assuming (1)-(4), any other point mapping to the generic point of Y would be a specialization of the generic point inside the fibre, which would contradict quasi-finiteness at the generic point; conversely the uniqueness condition holds for the morphism of schemes obtained above, which gives (1) by the scheme case.

Condition (6) (proof lines 660-662): it implies the equivalent conditions without further hypotheses because a finite morphism is quasi-finite, and conversely the equivalent conditions produce a nonempty open of the target over which the morphism is finite by the dense open finiteness lemma.
proof_roadmap: Pass to the schematic loci to reduce the first three conditions to the case of schemes.
Compare transcendence degrees and use finiteness implies quasi-finiteness to bring in quasi-finiteness at the generic point.
Identify the points over the generic point through specializations in the fibre, and finish with the finiteness-over-an-open statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of five conditions for a dominant locally of finite type morphism of integral algebraic spaces — vanishing of the transcendence degree at the generic points, finiteness of the residue field extension, finiteness over suitable nonempty affine opens, quasi-finiteness at the generic point, and uniqueness of the point over the generic point of the target — and, when the morphism is separated or quasi-compact, also finiteness over some nonempty open of the target (statement lines 603-624). The proof (proof lines 626-664) reduces the first three conditions to the case of schemes through the schematic loci, compares transcendence degrees, uses specializations in the fibre for the uniqueness condition, and finishes with the dense open finiteness lemma. H2: a six-condition equivalence with four inputs, written out in full.
